title: Sizzle Chef Rush
premise: A fast arcade kitchen game where the player taps frying pans to cook burger patties, waits for the ready moment, and serves a growing customer line before the food burns.
interaction_model: Single-screen pointer/touch timing play. Tap a pan once to begin cooking, tap it again during the ready window to serve, and tap burned pans to clear them.
objective: Serve as many waiting customers as possible for points while avoiding 3 burned-food misses.
progression: A run-based arcade loop with continuously spawning customers, rising pressure from queue buildup, and eventual failure after three mistakes. Progress is expressed through score rather than level advancement.
mood: Energetic, playful, hectic, and slightly stressful in a lighthearted way
likely_audience: players who enjoy short-session arcade reflex games
fans of simple cooking and restaurant-themed games
confidence_notes: High confidence that the core design is a cooking/timing arcade game because pan state changes, customer spawning, score gain, and miss-based failure are explicit in code.
Moderate confidence on the broader food-service framing because the customers all visually request the same burger-like item and there is no menu variation or restaurant upgrade layer.
High confidence that touch/mobile play is intended due to pointer input, full-screen canvas layout, and mobile-responsive UI rules.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished single-screen arcade cooking game called 'Sizzle Chef Rush' where the player runs a busy cartoon grill station using only tap or click controls. Show three frying pans along the bottom of the screen and a line of simple customers near the top, each effectively waiting for the same burger-style grilled item. The loop should be: tap an empty pan to start cooking, watch the food change from raw to cooked with a visible circular progress ring, wait for a clear green READY cue, then tap the ready pan again to serve the next customer in line for points. If the player waits too long after the item is ready, it burns, triggers a fail reaction, increments a miss counter, and the pan must be cleared before reuse. If the player serves when nobody is waiting, the food is wasted. Keep the session score-based and survival-focused with game over after 3 misses. Present everything in a colorful, exaggerated mobile-friendly arcade style with a fullscreen canvas, bold restaurant-themed typography, a visible HUD for score and misses, punchy sound effects, small celebratory or fail feedback animations, and a start screen plus game-over overlay. The experience should feel fast, readable, and replayable, emphasizing timing, multitasking across three pans, and managing customer demand under pressure rather than deep restaurant simulation.
